message.content: /seldon Gravelpost turns a folder of recipe text files into one printable cookbook PDF. The recipes sit in about two hundred plain-text and Markdown files with no common layout, so finding one means grepping, and printing one means copying it into a word processor first. The idea is a single Node command: `gravelpost build recipes/` reads every file, pulls out the title, ingredients and steps, and writes cookbook.pdf with a table of contents and an index by ingredient. Recipe apps want every recipe retyped into their own forms, and none of them builds an index by ingredient from loose files. Success is that all two hundred files build into one PDF without hand edits, and any recipe can be found from the index in under a minute. Scope is reading the folder, the PDF with its contents and index, and a warning list of files it couldn't parse. It won't fetch recipes from websites, because scrapers break every time a site changes its layout and the folder is the one source of truth. Later it might print a single recipe card on its own. Stakes are low: it's a weekend project, nothing depends on it, and the recipe files themselves are never changed.

content.text:
Gravelpost is a clear, contained idea, and your dump covers most of what a brief needs.

Recommended path: fast path

It says what the tool does, what it won't do and why, and how you'll know it works, and the stakes are low: a weekend project where the recipe files are never changed. I'll draft the brief myself and tag anything I have to guess with [ASSUMPTION] for you to check.

Does the fast path suit you, or would you rather I coach you through each decision one at a time?
